md_description: This workflow models preparation of primary rodent neuronal cultures, pharmacological treatment with neurotransmitter receptor antagonists, confocal laser scanning microscopy of synaptic junctions, and downstream computational analysis of postsynaptic density morphology. It preserves acquisition settings in the capture descriptions and produces raw 3D image stacks, segmented synaptic masks, morphology feature tables, and final comparative pathway-linked results.

rodent_brain_tissue.reasoning: This is an Entity node, so I included only intrinsic source-tissue metadata: organism/source identity, anatomy, and provenance of the donor tissue. I excluded culture, dissociation, plating, treatment, imaging, file, and computation fields because those belong to downstream Process, Capture, Signal, or Derivative nodes. No already_generated fields were provided here, so there were no explicit naming conflicts to avoid; I still kept the schema limited to non-overlapping source-tissue descriptors rather than repeating downstream sample or experiment identifiers.

md_schema.descr: Common organism name of the donor tissue source for the primary neuronal culture, recorded at the tissue-collection stage before dissociation or culture preparation. Example: rat or mouse. Use this to distinguish rodent source species when the exact strain is not the only identifying detail.
Scientific name of the donor organism for the brain tissue, recorded from the source animal at tissue collection. Example: Mus musculus or Rattus norvegicus.
Genetic strain or line of the donor rodent from which the brain tissue was obtained, recorded at the tissue-source stage. Example: C57BL/6J, Sprague Dawley, Wistar.

Age of the donor animal at the time brain tissue was collected, recorded before any culture preparation. Provide the unit in the value context used by the study, typically postnatal day (P) or weeks/months. Example: P0, P1, 8 weeks.
Biological sex of the donor animal supplying the brain tissue, recorded at the tissue-source stage. Example values: male, female, mixed, unknown.
Anatomical brain region from which the tissue was isolated for neuronal culture preparation, recorded at collection. Example: cortex, hippocampus, striatum, cerebellum.

More specific anatomical dissection detail for the collected brain tissue, if the workflow records a subregion or layer rather than only a broad brain region. Record at tissue collection before dissociation. Example: hippocampal CA1, cortical layer V.

Health or experimental status of the donor animal at tissue collection, if relevant to the source tissue provenance. Record as a concise status term before any culture manipulation. Example: healthy, diseased, transgenic, drug-exposed.

Method used to obtain the brain tissue from the donor animal, recorded at the source-tissue stage. Example: dissection, biopsy, surgical excision. Use only for the collection of the tissue itself, not later dissociation or plating.

Condition under which the brain tissue was held between collection and culture preparation, recorded as a provenance attribute of the source tissue. Example: fresh, ice_cold, cryopreserved, fixed. Do not use this for culture-incubation conditions.

culture_preparation.reasoning: This is a Process node, so I included only how the neuronal culture was prepared: isolation, dissociation, plating, maintenance conditions, timing, media, coating, and process quality/outcome indicators. I excluded donor tissue identity fields because those belong to the upstream Entity node, and I excluded imaging, file, segmentation, or analysis fields because those belong downstream. No already_generated fields were provided in this turn, so I focused on non-overlapping process descriptors that a downstream user would need to reproduce the primary neuronal culture preparation.

md_schema.descr: Method used to isolate neurons from the rodent brain tissue at the start of culture preparation. Record the technique applied before dissociation and plating. Example: mechanical, enzymatic, or combined isolation.

Enzyme or enzyme mix used to dissociate the brain tissue into a single-cell suspension during culture preparation. Record the reagent used at the dissociation step only. Example: papain, trypsin, collagenase.
Duration of the tissue dissociation step in minutes, measured during culture preparation. Typical range is about 5 to 60 minutes depending on tissue and enzyme conditions.

Number of neurons plated per square centimeter during the plating step of primary culture preparation. Measured at seeding onto coated culture vessels. Typical range may be from low thousands to tens of thousands cells/cm2.

Surface coating applied to the culture vessel before neuronal plating to support adhesion and neurite outgrowth. Record the coating used at the plating step. Example: poly-D-lysine, poly-L-lysine, laminin.

Basal or complete medium used to maintain the primary neuronal culture after plating. Record the maintenance medium composition at the culture-preparation stage. Example: Neurobasal, DMEM/F12, supplemented neuronal medium.

Whether serum was added to the neuronal culture medium during preparation or maintenance. Record the status applied during the culture step, not later treatment. Use true if serum was present, false if serum-free.
Temperature used to maintain the neuronal cultures during preparation and recovery after plating, measured in the incubator. Typical range for rodent primary neurons is about 35 to 37 celsius.
Carbon dioxide percentage used in the culture incubator during maintenance of the primary neuronal culture. Typical range is about 5 to 10 percent, commonly 5 percent.
Number of days the neuronal culture was maintained after plating and before downstream treatment or imaging. Measured in days in vitro (DIV) at the end of the preparation/maintenance period.

Qualitative outcome of the culture preparation step indicating whether neurons attached and maintained acceptable morphology/viability for downstream treatment. Record at the end of culture preparation. Example values: pass, borderline, fail.

primary_neuronal_culture.reasoning: This is an Entity node, so I included intrinsic culture-state metadata for the resulting primary neuronal culture: what it is, how old it is in vitro, its composition, viability/quality, and provenance links back to the source tissue and preparation context only as stable identifiers. I excluded procedure details from culture_preparation, treatment parameters, imaging settings, and any downstream file/analysis outputs. I also avoided repeating sample identifiers that are typically generated once at the root entity layer; no already_generated list was provided in this turn, so I kept the schema focused on culture properties rather than process descriptions.

md_schema.descr: Type of primary culture represented by this entity, recorded after preparation and before treatment or imaging. Use this to distinguish the biological culture state rather than the preparation protocol. Example: primary neuronal culture.
Culture age in days in vitro (DIV) at the time this neuronal culture entity is defined or sampled for downstream treatment/imaging. Typical range is 1 to 30 days depending on the experimental design.
Whether the culture is enriched for neurons relative to other brain-derived cells, as represented by this culture entity. Record at the point when the culture is ready for experimental use.

Estimated percentage of viable cells in the culture at the time the primary neuronal culture is assessed for experimental readiness. Measure at the culture-entity stage after preparation and before treatment. Typical range is 0 to 100 percent.

Estimated percentage of non-neuronal glial cells present in the culture when the primary neuronal culture is assessed. Measure as a composition attribute of the culture entity before treatment or imaging. Typical range is 0 to 100 percent.
Qualitative assessment of neuronal morphological maturity in the culture entity at the time of readiness for experiment. Record whether neurons show immature, developing, or mature morphology.

Operational readiness of the primary neuronal culture for downstream pharmacological treatment and confocal imaging, assessed at the entity stage after preparation. Example values: ready, not_ready, partially_ready.

Reference to the source brain tissue entity from which this primary neuronal culture was derived. Use a stable identifier or label if available, for example the rodent_brain_tissue node identifier or equivalent study-local reference.
Batch or lot label assigned to this culture entity during preparation, used to group cultures generated together from the same preparation event. Example: prep_batch_01.

Whether the culture entity was cryopreserved after preparation or maintained in fresh culture conditions. Record the storage state of the culture as an entity-level provenance attribute. Use true if cryopreserved, false if not.

control_branch_preparation.reasoning: This is a Process node, so I included only how the control branch was created from the primary neuronal culture and maintained as an untreated comparator. That means branch allocation, control condition designation, parallel maintenance duration, any vehicle handling, and a process-level quality flag. I excluded the upstream culture identity and the downstream control neuronal culture entity properties, because those belong to the Entity node, and I excluded treatment-antagonist details because those belong to the treated branch process. No already_generated fields were provided in this turn, so I avoided overlap by limiting the schema to control-branch process parameters rather than sample identity or imaging/analysis descriptors.

md_schema.descr: Method used to allocate the primary neuronal culture into the control branch, recorded at the start of the process. Example: split aliquot, parallel plate, matched replicate.
Type of untreated control condition established for the branch preparation step. Record the comparator state applied before imaging. Example values: untreated, vehicle_only, baseline.

Vehicle reagent used in the control branch if a vehicle-only comparator was maintained. Record the vehicle introduced during control preparation, not any downstream stain or imaging buffer. Example: DMSO, saline, PBS.
Final concentration of the vehicle in the control branch, if applicable, measured at the point of branch preparation. Typical range is 0 to a few percent depending on solvent use.
Duration for which the control branch was maintained in parallel with the treated samples prior to downstream imaging or analysis. Measured in hours at the end of the branch-preparation process.

Summary of incubation conditions used to maintain the control branch during the parallel-preparation period. Include only process-controlled conditions that match the treated branch. Example: same incubator settings as treated samples.
Strategy used to keep the control branch comparable to the treated samples during the preparation phase. Example values: same_batch, same_plate, matched_age, matched_density.

Operational quality assessment of the control branch preparation at the end of the process. Record whether the untreated comparator remained suitable for downstream imaging and analysis. Example values: pass, borderline, fail.

control_neuronal_culture.reasoning: I corrected the control_neuronal_culture Entity schema by removing the two field IDs that collide with already_generated DAG fields: in_vitro_age_days and glial_contamination_percent. I kept only non-duplicative intrinsic culture descriptors that still belong to this entity layer, such as control role, lineage, viability, purity, readiness, vessel identifier, replicate index, and cryostorage history. I did not introduce process, capture, or signal fields, and I avoided reusing semantically equivalent age/composition fields under alternate names.

md_schema.descr: Functional role of this neuronal culture entity within the workflow. Record that this entity serves as the untreated reference condition used for matched confocal microscopy comparisons.

Origin branch of the culture within the workflow, indicating that it was derived from the control branch preparation process rather than the treatment branch. Record as a simple lineage label at the entity stage.

Estimated percentage of viable cells in the control neuronal culture at the time it is used as the reference condition for confocal microscopy. Measure at the entity stage before imaging. Typical range is 0 to 100 percent.

Estimated fraction of neurons in the control culture relative to total cells, recorded as a culture-state attribute before imaging. Typical range is 0 to 100 percent and is used to characterize reference culture composition.
Operational readiness of the control neuronal culture for confocal microscopy, assessed after culture maintenance and before capture. Example values: ready, not_ready, compromised.

Identifier of the culture plate or vessel holding the control neuronal culture at the time it is prepared for confocal microscopy. Example format: plate_A1 or well_03. Use a stable local identifier if available.
Replicate index for the control culture within matched experimental sets, assigned at the entity stage to distinguish multiple control cultures from the same study. Example: 1, 2, 3.

Whether the control neuronal culture has a cryostorage history prior to being used as the reference imaging condition. Record only the state of the entity, not the storage protocol. Example values: never_cryopreserved, previously_cryopreserved.

neurotransmitter_antagonist_treatment.reasoning: This is a Process node describing pharmacological exposure, so I kept only treatment-operation fields needed to reproduce the antagonist application and assess process success. I removed the colliding field vehicle_used because it was already generated elsewhere in the DAG, and I avoided any other repeated or semantically equivalent reagent/vehicle identifiers. I also excluded culture identity, imaging settings, raw signal, and downstream analysis fields because those belong to other node types.

md_schema.descr: Name of the neurotransmitter receptor antagonist applied to the neuronal culture during the treatment step. Record the exact compound used for exposure. Example: CNQX, bicuculline, APV, gabazine.
Primary neurotransmitter receptor target or pathway antagonized by the compound, recorded at the treatment step. Example: AMPA receptor, GABA_A receptor, NMDA receptor, glycine receptor.

Final concentration of the antagonist used to expose the neuronal culture, measured in micromolar (uM) at the treatment step. Typical experimental range is often from nanomolar to tens of micromolar depending on compound and target.
Final concentration of the vehicle or solvent in the treatment condition at the time of antagonist exposure. Typical range is 0 to a few percent depending on solvent use.

Length of time the neuronal culture was exposed to the antagonist, measured in minutes from initiation to end of treatment. Typical range may be from minutes to hours depending on experimental design.
Temperature at which the antagonist exposure was carried out, measured during the treatment step. Typical range is near standard culture temperature, around 35 to 37 celsius.
Whether a washout step was performed after antagonist exposure and before downstream imaging or further handling. Use this only to describe the treatment process, not imaging preparation.
Recovery time allowed after antagonist exposure before the next workflow step, measured in minutes. Record at the end of the treatment process if applicable.
Operational assessment of whether the antagonist treatment was successfully applied as intended, recorded at the end of the process. Example values: pass, borderline, fail.

treated_neuronal_culture.reasoning: This is an Entity node, so I kept only intrinsic post-treatment culture attributes that remain meaningful as properties of the treated sample before capture. I excluded upstream treatment-process variables and downstream imaging/analysis fields. I also removed the previously colliding field ids culture_role and imaging_readiness_status, and avoided semantically equivalent duplicates of control/treated role labeling or readiness status. The remaining fields describe the treated culture’s condition, provenance, vessel context, and replicate identity without overlapping earlier DAG steps.

md_schema.descr: State of the neuronal culture after antagonist exposure and before imaging, recorded as an entity attribute. Example values: treated, recovered, partially_recovered, stressed.

Workflow branch from which this culture entity originates, indicating that it was produced by the antagonist treatment process rather than the control branch. Record as a stable lineage label at the entity stage.

Identifier of the plate, dish, chamber, or well holding the treated neuronal culture at the time it is prepared for confocal microscopy. Example format: plate_B2, well_05, chamber_1. Use a stable local identifier if available.
Estimated percentage of viable cells in the treated neuronal culture after antagonist exposure and before imaging. Measure at the entity stage after treatment. Typical range is 0 to 100 percent.
Qualitative assessment of whether the treated culture retains acceptable neuronal morphology for imaging, recorded before confocal capture. Example values: intact, partially_degraded, degraded.
Replicate index for this treated culture within the experiment, assigned at the entity stage to distinguish multiple treated samples. Example: 1, 2, 3.
Whether the treated culture underwent and completed a recovery period before imaging, recorded as a stable entity attribute. Example values: completed, not_completed, unknown.

Whether the treated neuronal culture was fixed prior to confocal microscopy. Record only the entity state immediately before capture; do not use this for fixation protocol details. Example values: fixed, live, unknown.

Type of container or culture vessel used to hold the treated neuronal culture before confocal microscopy. Record the vessel form as an entity-level attribute, not the imaging instrument. Example values: glass_bottom_dish, multiwell_plate, chamber_slide.

Duration for which the treated culture was held in its prepared state before confocal imaging, measured in hours at the entity stage. Use this to capture short pre-capture holding time, not treatment exposure duration.

confocal_microscopy_capture_treated.reasoning: This is a Capture node, so I included only the measurement-session and instrument-configuration metadata for the treated confocal acquisition: microscope and software identity, objective and optics settings, laser/channel settings, scanning and z-stack parameters, detector settings, and capture-level quality/readout details. I excluded biological sample properties because those belong to the treated neuronal culture entity, and I excluded raw file properties because those belong to the resulting Signal node. I also avoided previously generated fields in the DAG, including culture_role and imaging_readiness_status, and limited the schema to capture settings that a downstream user would need to reproduce the treated imaging session.

md_schema.descr: Manufacturer of the confocal laser scanning microscope used for the treated imaging capture session. Record the hardware vendor at the time of acquisition. Example: Leica, Zeiss, Nikon, Olympus.
Model name or number of the confocal laser scanning microscope used for the treated capture session. Record the specific instrument configuration used for imaging. Example: LSM 880, A1R, SP8.
Serial number of the confocal microscope used for the treated acquisition session, recorded for instrument traceability. Use the hardware serial if available, in a stable string format.
Name of the acquisition software used to control the confocal imaging session for treated neurons. Example: ZEN, LAS X, NIS-Elements, FV10-ASW.
Version of the acquisition software used during the treated confocal capture session. Record the exact software version at acquisition time, such as 3.6, 4.1, or a full build string if available.
Objective magnification used for the treated confocal capture session, recorded as a numeric multiplier. Typical values may include 40x, 60x, or 100x. Measure/record at the time of acquisition.
Numerical aperture of the objective lens used for treated imaging, recorded at the capture session. Typical range is approximately 0.6 to 1.4 depending on the objective.
Excitation laser wavelength or wavelengths used during the treated confocal capture session, recorded in nanometers. Provide the set used for the imaging channels, such as 488, 561, and 633 nm.

Laser power used for treated confocal acquisition, expressed as a percentage of the configured output at the microscope. Record at the moment of imaging. Typical range is 0 to 100 percent, often much lower in practice.

Confocal pinhole size used during the treated capture session, recorded in Airy units. This is an acquisition setting that affects optical section thickness. Typical range is about 0.5 to 2.0 Airy units.

Axial step size used for the treated 3D confocal z-stack acquisition, measured in micrometers per slice. Record at capture time. Typical range is about 0.1 to 2.0 micrometers depending on resolution needs.
Scanning mode used during the treated confocal acquisition session. Record the operational mode selected in the instrument software. Example values: sequential, line, frame, xyz_stack.
Detector type used for treated confocal image acquisition. Record the configured detector hardware responsible for signal collection. Example: PMT, HyD, GaAsP.

In-plane pixel size of the treated confocal acquisition in micrometers per pixel, defined by the selected objective and zoom settings at capture. Typical range may be about 0.02 to 1.0 micrometers per pixel depending on resolution.
Number of line averages applied during the treated confocal capture session to improve signal quality. Record the acquisition setting used on the microscope. Typical values are 1 or greater.

Operational quality assessment of the treated confocal acquisition session, based on whether the image was acquired with acceptable focus, signal, and coverage for downstream analysis. Example values: pass, borderline, fail.

confocal_microscopy_capture_control.reasoning: This is a Capture node, so I still stayed in the instrument-configuration territory, but I removed every field that had already been generated elsewhere in the DAG, including all generic microscope, software, and acquisition-setting names. To avoid collisions, I used capture-specific fields that describe the treated session without reusing prior identifiers: channel-specific settings, scan geometry, depth range, and capture-specific QC. I excluded sample, raw-file, and downstream-analysis properties because those belong to other node types.

md_schema.descr: Number of fluorescence or reflected-light channels configured for the treated confocal acquisition session. Record at the time of capture. Typical values are 1 to 4 depending on the labeling scheme.

Emission detection bands used for the treated confocal session, recorded in nanometers as the configured channel set. Provide the set used for image collection, such as 500-550, 570-620, or equivalent band descriptions.

Total axial thickness covered by the treated 3D confocal z-stack, measured in micrometers from first to last optical section. Record at capture time. Typical range may be a few to several tens of micrometers depending on specimen thickness.
Lateral image dimensions of the treated confocal frame or stack, recorded as pixel counts in x by y at acquisition. Example format: 1024x1024 or 2048x2048.
Bit depth of the treated confocal acquisition, indicating the intensity encoding depth of the raw detector output. Typical values are 8, 12, or 16 bits.

Detector gain or amplification setting used during the treated capture session, recorded as an instrument setting at acquisition time. Use the native unit or numeric value reported by the instrument software.
Detector offset or background baseline setting used during the treated confocal acquisition. Record the value applied at capture time to define the signal baseline and avoid clipping.
Scan speed or dwell-related acquisition setting used for the treated confocal session, recorded as configured on the microscope. Use the native instrument value if available.
Whether the treated confocal acquisition used tile scanning to cover a larger field of view. Use true if a tiled mosaic was acquired, false otherwise.

Quality flag indicating whether focus remained stable throughout the treated confocal acquisition session. Record at the end of capture. Use true if focus was acceptable across the acquired volume, false if focus drift compromised the session.

raw_confocal_stack_treated.reasoning: This is a Signal node, so I kept the schema strictly on raw-file properties and avoided the previously colliding field id bit_depth. I included file format, size, dimensions, channel/depth structure, storage location, and integrity/quality descriptors that characterize the raw treated confocal stack itself. I excluded capture settings, biological culture attributes, and downstream computed features because those belong to other node types. The schema is intentionally minimal and non-overlapping with earlier generated metadata.

md_schema.descr: File format of the raw treated confocal image stack as stored on disk or in the archive. Record the technical container format for the signal artefact. Example: .czi, .lif, .tif, .nd2.
Size of the raw treated confocal stack file in bytes, measured for the stored artefact after acquisition and export. Typical values can range from megabytes to many gigabytes for 3D stacks.

In-plane pixel dimensions of the raw treated confocal image stack, recorded as width by height in pixels for the stored signal artefact. Measure from the file contents rather than from microscope settings.
Number of axial slices in the raw treated confocal stack, measured from the stored image file. Record the depth of the 3D stack as an integer count.
Number of imaging channels present in the raw treated confocal stack, measured from the stored file. Typical values depend on the number of fluorophores and detector channels used.
Whether compression was applied to the raw treated confocal stack file when stored or exported. Record only the file-level state, not the acquisition settings. Example values: none, lossless, lossy.
Filesystem or archive path where the raw treated confocal stack is stored. Provide the location of the raw signal artefact, such as a project directory or object-store URI.
Checksum or hash value used to verify integrity of the raw treated confocal stack file. Record the value used for file-level provenance, for example an MD5 or SHA-256 hash string.

Technical integrity assessment of the raw treated confocal stack after acquisition and storage. Record whether the file appears complete and readable. Example values: valid, corrupted, partial, unknown.

raw_confocal_stack_control.reasoning: This is a Signal node, so I avoided the previously generated raw-stack field names reported as collisions and instead selected a different set of raw-file technical descriptors that still stay within Signal territory: dimensionality, channel metadata, microscopy file organization, provenance, and archive-level integrity. I excluded capture settings and downstream analytical interpretation. The remaining fields are framed as file-level properties of the treated raw confocal stack only, with no overlap with Entity, Process, Capture, or Derivative nodes.

md_schema.descr: Whether the raw treated confocal signal is stored as a three-dimensional stack rather than a single 2D plane. Record this at the file level after acquisition/export. Use true for z-stacks and false for single-plane images.
Number of timepoints in the raw treated confocal signal if the file is a multi-timepoint series. Record the file-level temporal dimensionality after acquisition. Use 1 if no time series is present.

Names or labels of the imaging channels present in the raw treated confocal stack, recorded from the file metadata. Example: DAPI, GFP, Alexa488, Alexa568. Use a delimiter-separated string if multiple channels are present.

X-axis voxel size of the raw treated confocal signal in micrometers per pixel, measured from file metadata. This is a file-level spatial resolution property, not the microscope setting. Typical values depend on zoom and objective.

Y-axis voxel size of the raw treated confocal signal in micrometers per pixel, measured from file metadata. This is a file-level spatial resolution property, not the microscope setting. Typical values depend on zoom and objective.
Z-axis voxel spacing of the raw treated confocal signal in micrometers per slice, measured from file metadata. This describes the stored 3D sampling interval, not the acquisition control settings.

Reference to the capture session that produced this raw treated confocal stack, stored as a stable local identifier or node label if available. Use this to link the signal file back to its capture provenance without repeating capture settings.

Name of the software used to export or convert the raw treated confocal signal file, if different from the acquisition software. Record the file-handling tool applied after capture. Example: vendor exporter, ImageJ, Fiji, OMERO export.
Version of the software used to export or convert the raw treated confocal signal file, if applicable. Record the exact version string used for file handling after capture.

Assessment of whether the archived raw treated confocal signal is complete and accessible in its storage location. Record the file/archive state after transfer or archiving. Example values: archived, missing, incomplete, inaccessible.

image_stack_organization_treated.reasoning: This is a Process node, so I included only computational reformatting and organization details for the treated raw confocal stack: software identity, version, algorithm or workflow, channel/order handling, resampling or normalization settings, and process-level output quality. I excluded raw file properties because those belong to the upstream Signal node, and I excluded segmentation or morphology because those belong to later Derivative nodes. I also avoided all previously generated field names from earlier steps, including capture-layer and signal-layer collisions reported by the user, and kept the schema focused on the assembly/formatting operation itself.

md_schema.descr: Name of the software or pipeline used to assemble and format the treated raw confocal data into an analyzable image stack. Record the exact tool used for this computational organization step. Example: FIJI, ImageJ, Python pipeline, vendor converter.
Version of the software or pipeline used for treated image-stack organization. Record the exact version or release used at this process step, such as 1.53, 2.0.1, or a commit-tagged release.

Name of the algorithm, script, or conversion routine used to organize the treated raw confocal data into an analyzable stack. Example: channel_merge, z_order_sort, vendor_export_to_ome_tiff, custom_preprocessing.

Number of raw treated confocal stacks ingested into this organization process. Record the count of input signal files or stacks combined into the analyzable output. Typical value is 1 for a direct reformatting step.
File or container format produced by the treated image-stack organization step, recorded as the analyzable representation after computational formatting. Example: OME-TIFF, NIfTI, TIFF stack, HDF5.
Channel ordering convention applied when assembling the treated analyzable stack, recorded at the organization step. Example values: acquisition_order, wavelength_order, fixed_channel_map.

Orientation convention used for the z axis after organization of the treated stack. Record how the computational step defines slice order relative to acquisition. Example values: top_to_bottom, bottom_to_top, acquisition_native.

Whether intensity normalization or rescaling was applied during treated image-stack organization. Record only the process-level transformation status, not downstream analysis normalization. Example values: true or false.
Whether spatial or axial resampling was applied while organizing the treated raw confocal data into the analyzable stack. Use this to record format/geometry conversion performed at this process step.

Operational quality assessment of the treated stack produced by the organization step, based on whether the output is correctly assembled, readable, and suitable for downstream segmentation. Example values: pass, borderline, fail.

image_stack_organization_control.reasoning: This is a Process node, so I included only computational reformatting and organization details for the control raw confocal stack, but all obvious organization fields were already used by earlier DAG steps. To avoid collisions, I generated a new set of process-specific fields that still describe the same semantic territory: input/output relationship, stack indexing conventions, metadata-preservation behavior, and QC of the organization operation. I excluded raw signal properties, capture settings, and downstream derivative interpretation.

md_schema.descr: Reference identifier or filename of the raw control confocal stack ingested by this organization process. Use the local file label or archive reference for the input signal artefact, not a biological sample identifier.
Reference identifier or filename assigned to the organized control image stack after computational formatting. Record the output artefact label created by this process.

Rule used to order z slices during organization of the control raw confocal stack. Record the computational convention applied to assemble the analyzable stack. Example values: acquisition_order, ascending_z, descending_z, vendor_native.

Whether multiple imaging channels from the control raw confocal data were merged during organization or kept separate in the analyzable stack. Record the process-level handling of channels. Example values: true or false.

Whether the control image stack axes were reoriented during organization to match an internal analysis convention. Record only whether a reorientation occurred, not the capture geometry. Example values: true or false.

Whether original acquisition metadata were preserved, copied, or stripped during the control stack organization step. Record the handling of embedded metadata in the processed output. Example values: preserved, partially_preserved, stripped.
Runtime of the control image-stack organization process in seconds, measured for the computational assembly step. Record the wall-clock time required to convert raw data into the analyzable stack.

Whether the organized control image stack passed a basic post-processing sanity check for readability and expected structure. Record the process-level verification outcome. Example values: true or false.

Free-text note describing any nonstandard format conversion or re-encoding performed during control stack organization. Use this only when a concise note is needed to interpret the computational formatting step.

Name or identifier of the person or automated account that executed the control image-stack organization step, if tracked in the workflow provenance. Use a local operator label rather than a sample identifier.

treated_analyzable_stack.reasoning: This is a Derivative node, so I included only computed-output metadata for the treated analyzable stack: the transformation workflow applied to the raw image stack, key processing parameters, output dimensionality/representation, and derivative-specific quality indicators. I excluded raw file/storage properties because those belong to the Signal node, and I excluded capture settings because those belong to the Capture node. I also avoided previously generated field names from earlier organization/capture/signal steps, keeping the schema focused on the computed stack as an intermediate analysis product rather than its inputs.

md_schema.descr: Name of the software or pipeline used to produce the treated analyzable stack from the organized image data. Record the computational tool used for this derivative generation step. Example: FIJI, CellProfiler, Python notebook, custom pipeline.
Version of the software or pipeline used to produce the treated analyzable stack. Record the exact version or release used for this derivative step, such as 1.53, 2.0.1, or a commit-tagged release.
Name of the algorithm or workflow used to generate the treated analyzable stack. Example: normalization_pipeline, stack_preparation, denoising, alignment, custom_presegmentation.

Reference to the organized treated image stack used as input for this derivative step. Use a stable local identifier or provenance label for the source stack rather than a file path. Example: treated_analyzable_stack_input_01.
Whether denoising was applied during generation of the treated analyzable stack. Record the presence of a preprocessing step that improves downstream segmentation readiness.
Whether contrast normalization or intensity scaling was applied during generation of the treated analyzable stack. This records derivative-level preprocessing, not acquisition settings.

Effective voxel size of the treated analyzable stack after derivative processing, measured in micrometers along x, y, and z if available. Record the output spatial resolution used for downstream segmentation and quantification. Typical values depend on the original acquisition and any resampling.
Number of z slices in the treated analyzable stack after derivative processing, recorded as the output dimensionality of this computed product.
Operational assessment of whether the treated analyzable stack is suitable for downstream synaptic segmentation and morphology quantification. Example values: ready, borderline, unsuitable.

Numeric quality score assigned to the treated analyzable stack after preprocessing, if the workflow evaluates computational output quality. Record the score used by the pipeline at the end of this derivative step. Typical range may be 0 to 1 or 0 to 100 depending on implementation.

control_analyzable_stack.reasoning: This is a Derivative node, but the previously used generic derivation fields are all already taken elsewhere in the DAG. So I kept only control-specific computed-output metadata that does not collide: the tissue/condition-specific computational product identity, postprocessing dimensions, segmentation suitability, and comparison linkage to the matched treated output. I excluded raw file, capture, and upstream process details, and I also avoided the generic derivation field names called out in the collision errors.

md_schema.descr: Type of computed control image product represented by this derivative node, recorded after processing and before segmentation or morphology extraction. Example: analyzable_stack, presegmentation_stack, normalized_stack.

Effective voxel size of the control analyzable stack after any derivative resampling, measured in micrometers and recorded at the output of this node. Use this to describe the computed stack geometry rather than the original acquisition geometry. Typical values depend on resampling choices.

Number of z slices present in the control computed stack after derivative processing, recorded at the output of this node. This captures the dimensionality of the produced control analysis-ready image stack.

Number of channels retained in the control computed stack after derivative processing, recorded at the output of this node. Use this to describe the output stack composition if channels were dropped, merged, or reordered.

Assessment of whether the control computed stack is suitable for downstream synaptic segmentation and morphology quantification, recorded at the end of this derivative step. Example values: suitable, borderline, unsuitable.

Whether obvious processing artifacts were detected in the control computed stack, such as clipping, tiling seams, or interpolation artifacts, at the end of this derivative step. Use this as a derivative quality indicator specific to the control output.

Reference identifier for the matched treated output or comparison set that the control computed stack was prepared against, if the workflow preserves a pairing link at the derivative stage. Example: treated_analyzable_stack pair label or comparison group ID.
Container or serialization format of the control computed stack after derivative processing, recorded at the output of this node. Example: OME-TIFF, NIfTI, HDF5, TIFF stack.

Whether the control computed stack was successfully exported and is available for downstream segmentation or analysis. Record the derivative output state rather than storage path. Example values: exported, pending_export, export_failed.

postsynaptic_density_segmentation_treate.reasoning: This is a Process node, so I included only the segmentation-operation metadata for the treated stack: segmentation software identity, version, algorithm type, input reference, key threshold or model parameters, and process-level segmentation quality. I excluded raw and derivative file properties because those belong to the input Signal/Derivative nodes, and I excluded final mask artefact properties because those belong to the treated_synaptic_mask output node. I also avoided previously generated field names from earlier computational steps that the user reported as collisions, keeping the schema limited to the act of segmenting postsynaptic density structures in the treated images.

md_schema.descr: Name of the software or pipeline used to segment postsynaptic density and synaptic junction structures in the treated image stack. Record the exact computational tool used for this process step. Example: CellProfiler, FIJI, Ilastik, custom Python pipeline.

Version of the segmentation software or pipeline used for treated image-stack segmentation. Record the exact version or release used at this process step, such as 1.53, 2.0.1, or a commit-tagged release.
Name of the segmentation algorithm or workflow used to identify postsynaptic density structures in the treated stack. Example: thresholding, watershed, random_forest, UNet, custom_rule_based.

Reference to the treated analyzable stack used as input to the segmentation process. Use a stable local identifier or provenance label for the source stack rather than a file path. Example: treated_analyzable_stack_01.

Numeric threshold used by the segmentation process when applicable, recorded at the treated segmentation step. Provide the value in the intensity scale or probability scale used by the algorithm. Typical range depends on the method and image normalization.

Probability cutoff used when a machine-learning or probabilistic segmentation model is applied to treated image stacks. Record the decision threshold at the process step if applicable. Typical range is 0 to 1.

Minimum object size retained during treated segmentation, measured in pixels or voxels according to the algorithm implementation. Record the filtering threshold used to suppress small spurious detections.
Whether smoothing or contour regularization was applied during treated segmentation prior to mask output. Record the presence of a post-processing step at the segmentation process.

Operational quality assessment of the treated segmentation process, based on whether postsynaptic density structures were identified consistently and with acceptable accuracy for downstream quantification. Example values: pass, borderline, fail.
Execution time of the treated segmentation process in seconds, measured for the computational identification step. Typical values depend on stack size and algorithm complexity.

postsynaptic_density_segmentation_contro.reasoning: This is a Process node, so I included only segmentation-operation metadata for the control stack, but I had to avoid every previously generated segmentation field-id collision reported by the user. To stay within the node’s territory without reusing those ids, I used new fields for the process input/output context and process controls that are still about segmentation execution, while excluding raw stack properties and final mask artefact properties. I also avoided semantically equivalent duplicates of already-generated segmentation software, thresholds, and quality fields by shifting to alternative process descriptors that a downstream user would still need to reproduce the step.

md_schema.descr: Concise textual summary of how postsynaptic density and synaptic junction structures were identified in the control image stack at this process step. Describe the operational approach used by the segmentation workflow, for example classical thresholding, atlas-guided detection, or deep-learning-based labeling.

Reference to the labeled dataset, model corpus, or annotation source used to train a segmentation model, if applicable, for the control segmentation step. Use a stable local or study reference rather than a file path.

Decision threshold applied to model-based inference scores during control segmentation, recorded as the cutoff used to accept candidate synaptic structures. Typical range is 0 to 1 for probability-based models.

List or summary of postprocessing operations applied to the control segmentation results before mask output. Example operations: hole filling, connected-component filtering, edge cleanup, watershed refinement.
Whether the control segmentation result was manually reviewed after automated processing and before mask generation. Use this to record human oversight of the process output.

Whether boundary refinement or contour adjustment was applied to the control segmentation output as part of the process step. This records a segmentation-specific cleanup operation, not downstream morphology extraction.
Number of candidate postsynaptic density objects accepted by the control segmentation process before the final mask was passed downstream. Record the count produced by the process.
Number of candidate objects rejected during control segmentation because they failed the process criteria. Record the count at the end of segmentation.
Execution mode used for the control segmentation workflow. Record whether the process ran interactively, in batch mode, or via a scripted pipeline.

Free-text notes about any unusual conditions, warnings, or implementation details relevant to the control segmentation step. Use this for process-specific remarks that are not captured by the other fields.

treated_synaptic_mask.reasoning: This is a Derivative node, so I included only properties of the computed mask itself: mask file representation, dimensions, sparsity/coverage, mask quality, and provenance to the segmentation process. I excluded the segmentation algorithm settings because those belong to the upstream Process node, and I excluded raw image/capture properties because those belong to Signal and Capture nodes. I also avoided previously generated field names from earlier steps, including the segmentation-layer names reported as collisions, and focused on the treated mask as a derived artefact rather than its inputs.

md_schema.descr: File or container format of the treated synaptic mask as stored on disk or in the archive. Record the technical representation of the derivative artefact. Example: .tif, .png, .npy, .h5.

In-plane pixel dimensions of the treated synaptic mask, recorded as width by height in pixels for the stored derivative artefact. If the mask is 3D, include the z dimension in the same string representation. Example: 1024x1024 or 1024x1024x48.

Total number of voxels or pixels labeled as foreground in the treated synaptic mask, measured from the derivative output. Use this as a compact size measure of the segmented synaptic structure content.
Percentage of the treated analyzable stack occupied by foreground mask pixels or voxels, measured from the derivative output. Typical range is 0 to 100 percent and reflects segmentation extent.

Semantic class represented by the treated mask, recorded as a derivative label. For this workflow the expected class is synaptic_structure or a closely related label used by the segmentation pipeline.

Reference to the segmentation process that generated the treated synaptic mask, recorded as a stable provenance label or node reference rather than a parameter list. Example: postsynaptic_density_segmentation_treated.

Technical integrity assessment of the treated synaptic mask file after generation and storage. Record whether the derivative artefact is complete and readable. Example values: valid, corrupted, partial, unknown.

Numeric measure of boundary regularity or smoothness of the treated mask, if calculated as a derivative quality metric. Record the score used by the workflow at the output stage. Typical range depends on implementation.
Number of disconnected foreground components present in the treated synaptic mask, measured from the derivative output. This helps characterize segmentation fragmentation.

Operational quality assessment of the treated synaptic mask output, based on whether the derived segmentation is suitable for downstream morphology quantification. Example values: pass, borderline, fail.

control_synaptic_mask.reasoning: This is a Derivative node, so I kept the schema on computed mask characteristics rather than raw or capture settings. However, because all previously used generic mask field IDs collide across the DAG, I renamed the control-mask metadata with control-specific prefixes and retained only derivative-level properties: storage/representation, size/shape, segmentation extent, provenance reference, integrity, and quality. I excluded upstream segmentation parameters and downstream morphology outputs because they belong to other nodes.

md_schema.descr: File or container format used to store the control synaptic mask derivative. Record the technical representation of the mask artefact on disk. Example: .tif, .png, .npy, .h5.

In-plane pixel dimensions of the control synaptic mask, recorded as width by height in pixels for the stored derivative artefact. If the mask is 3D, include the z dimension in the same string representation. Example: 1024x1024 or 1024x1024x48.
Total number of voxels or pixels labeled as foreground in the control synaptic mask, measured from the derivative output. Use this as a compact size measure of segmented synaptic structure content.
Percentage of the control analyzable stack occupied by foreground mask pixels or voxels, measured from the derivative output. Typical range is 0 to 100 percent and reflects segmentation extent.

Semantic class represented by the control mask, recorded as a derivative label. For this workflow the expected class is synaptic_structure or a closely related label used by the segmentation pipeline.

Reference to the segmentation process that generated the control synaptic mask, recorded as a stable provenance label or node reference rather than a parameter list. Example: postsynaptic_density_segmentation_control.

Technical integrity assessment of the control synaptic mask file after generation and storage. Record whether the derivative artefact is complete and readable. Example values: valid, corrupted, partial, unknown.

Numeric measure of boundary regularity or smoothness of the control mask, if calculated as a derivative quality metric. Record the score used by the workflow at the output stage. Typical range depends on implementation.
Number of disconnected foreground components present in the control synaptic mask, measured from the derivative output. This helps characterize segmentation fragmentation.

Operational quality assessment of the control synaptic mask output, based on whether the derived segmentation is suitable for downstream morphology quantification. Example values: pass, borderline, fail.

morphology_quantification_treated.reasoning: This is a Process node, so I included only the measurement-operation metadata for treated synaptic morphology quantification: software identity, version, metric definitions, key measurement scales, normalization settings, and process-level output quality. I excluded mask file properties because those belong to the upstream Derivative node, and I excluded final table/file properties because those belong to the treated_morphology_table output node. I also avoided previously generated field names from earlier workflow steps that were reported as collisions, and I kept the schema focused on how morphology was quantified rather than on the resulting values themselves.

md_schema.descr: Name of the software or pipeline used to quantify synaptic morphology in the treated samples. Record the exact computational tool used for this process step. Example: FIJI, CellProfiler, Python pipeline, custom statistics workflow.
Version of the software or pipeline used for treated morphology quantification. Record the exact version or release used at this process step, such as 1.53, 2.0.1, or a commit-tagged release.
Name of the algorithm or workflow used to compute synaptic morphology features from the treated mask. Example: feature_extraction, shape_metrics, junction_geometry, custom_measurement_pipeline.

Reference to the treated synaptic mask used as input for the morphology quantification process. Use a stable local identifier or provenance label for the source mask rather than a file path. Example: treated_synaptic_mask_01.

Name of the synaptic morphology feature set computed for the treated samples. Record the set of measurements extracted by the process. Example: PSD_size_shape_geometry, synapse_shape_panel, custom_feature_panel.
Unit system used for the treated morphology measurements, recorded at the quantification step. Example values: micrometers, pixels, arbitrary_units, normalized_units.

Normalization method applied to treated morphology measurements before output, if any. Record the process-level scaling or correction method used. Example: none, per_cell, per_field, z_score, area_normalized.

Minimum postsynaptic density area retained during treated morphology quantification, measured in the unit system used by the pipeline. Record the filtering threshold applied to define valid objects or features.
Set of shape descriptors calculated for treated synaptic objects during quantification. Example values: area, perimeter, circularity, aspect_ratio, solidity, eccentricity.
Operational assessment of the treated morphology quantification process, based on whether the computed measurements are suitable for downstream comparison. Example values: pass, borderline, fail.
Execution time of the treated morphology quantification process in seconds, measured for the computational feature-extraction step. Typical values depend on number of objects and feature complexity.

morphology_quantification_control.reasoning: This is a Derivative node, so I included only computed-result metadata for the control morphology table: table/file representation, row/column structure, feature scope, statistical summary coverage, and output quality. I excluded the quantification procedure itself because that belongs to the upstream Process node, and I excluded raw mask or capture properties because those belong to upstream Derivative/Signal/Capture nodes. I also avoided all previously generated quantification-layer field names reported as collisions, and kept the schema focused on the output table as a reusable derived result.

md_schema.descr: File or container format of the control morphology table as stored on disk or in the archive. Record the technical representation of the derived results table. Example: .csv, .tsv, .xlsx, .parquet, .h5.

Number of rows in the control morphology table, measured from the stored derived result. Typically corresponds to the number of segmented objects, fields of view, or cell-level units included in the table.
Number of columns in the control morphology table, measured from the stored derived result. Typically reflects the number of quantified synaptic features plus identifiers and QC fields.

Name of the column schema or feature layout used in the control morphology table. Record the panel of quantified measurements without repeating the process used to calculate them. Example: synaptic_morphology_feature_panel, PSD_metrics_v1, custom_feature_schema.

Scope of summary statistics represented in the control morphology table. Record whether the table contains per-object measurements, per-cell summaries, per-image summaries, or aggregated condition-level summaries. Example values: per_object, per_cell, per_image, aggregated_condition.
Encoding used in the control morphology table for missing or not-applicable values. Record the stored convention used in the derived table. Example: NA, NaN, blank, -9999.
Checksum or hash value used to verify integrity of the control morphology table file. Record the value used for file-level provenance, for example an MD5 or SHA-256 hash string.
Filesystem or archive path where the control morphology table is stored. Provide the location of the derived results table, such as a project directory or object-store URI.

Technical integrity assessment of the control morphology table after generation and storage. Record whether the derived table is complete and readable. Example values: valid, corrupted, partial, unknown.

Operational quality assessment of the control morphology table output, based on whether the derived measurements are complete and suitable for downstream comparative analysis. Example values: pass, borderline, fail.

treated_morphology_table.reasoning: This is a Derivative node, so I kept the schema limited to the treated morphology table as a computed artefact and avoided the collided ids table_row_count and table_column_count. I included storage, provenance, content-organization, and readiness details that remain useful without duplicating earlier fields. I excluded quantification-process details because those belong upstream, and I excluded raw masks/capture properties because those belong earlier in the DAG.

md_schema.descr: Storage or serialization format of the treated morphology feature table as exported by the pipeline. Record the technical representation of the derivative table artefact. Example: csv, tsv, xlsx, parquet, json.
Filesystem path, object-store URI, or archive location where the treated morphology table is stored. Record the location of the derivative table artefact, not the upstream raw data or mask.
Label for the feature group or namespace represented in the treated morphology table. Record the feature family captured by the table, such as PSD geometry or synaptic shape metrics.
Keying scheme used to organize rows in the treated morphology table. Record how each row is identified for downstream analysis. Example values: by_synapse, by_cell, by_field_of_view, by_sample.
Sort order used in the treated morphology table export, if rows were intentionally ordered. Example values: acquisition_order, sample_order, ascending_feature_value, none.

Level at which values in the treated morphology table are summarized. Record whether the table contains object-level measurements or aggregated summaries. Example values: per_object, per_sample, per_field_of_view, mixed.
Version or release of the feature schema used in the treated morphology table. Record the column-definition schema version at export time, such as v1, 2024.1, or a pipeline-specific tag.
Checksum or hash value used to verify the integrity of the treated morphology table file after export. Record the value used for file-level provenance, for example an MD5 or SHA-256 string.
Operational readiness of the treated morphology table for downstream statistics or comparative analysis, assessed after export. Example values: ready, borderline, unsuitable.
Timestamp when the treated morphology table was exported or finalized, recorded as a derivative provenance attribute. Use a machine-readable date-time string if available, e.g. 2026-08-18T12:34:56Z.

control_morphology_table.reasoning: This is a Derivative node, so I kept only non-colliding, table-level descriptors for the control morphology table and removed the previously reported export_timestamp collision. I focused on table identity, content composition, column structure, missing-value and outlier policies, standardization, notes, reproducibility tags, and grouping scheme because these describe the derivative artefact without repeating upstream quantification or downstream comparison fields. I also avoided any raw signal, mask, or capture metadata.

md_schema.descr: Stable local identifier assigned to the control morphology table derivative artefact. Use a study-local table label or accession-like string, for example control_morphology_table_v1. This identifies the table output without duplicating file storage details.

Number of morphology feature columns recorded in the control table, excluding identifier columns and purely administrative metadata. Record the content width of the table as a downstream-useful summary. Typical values depend on the feature panel used.
Name of the column used to uniquely identify each row in the control morphology table. Example values: synapse_id, cell_id, field_of_view_id, sample_id.

Policy used to represent or handle missing values in the control morphology table. Example values: blank, NA, null, imputed, filtered. Record the table-level convention used in the exported derivative.

Policy used to handle outlier measurements in the control morphology table, if any. Example values: none, winsorized, removed, flagged, transformed. Record the table-level convention used for the exported feature set.
Whether measurement units were standardized across the columns in the control morphology table before export. Use this to indicate consistent output formatting at the derivative-table stage.

Free-text notes describing any table-level caveats for the control morphology derivative, such as merged feature groups, excluded rows, or export warnings. Keep this limited to the table artefact itself, not the upstream measurement process.
Short reproducibility tag or digest for the control morphology table version, used to distinguish exports produced from the same analysis pipeline. Example: analysis_run_07, export_batch_A.
Scheme used to group columns in the control morphology table for human or programmatic interpretation. Example values: flat, grouped_by_feature_family, hierarchical, multiindex.

Brief provenance note describing the origin of the control morphology table derivative, such as the analysis branch, input mask family, or export context. Keep this as a table-level lineage note rather than a process parameter list.

comparative_synaptic_analysis.reasoning: This is a Process node, so I included only comparative-analysis operation metadata: analysis software identity, statistical test family, model specification, comparison design, multiple-testing control, effect-size reporting, and process-level result quality. I excluded upstream feature-table contents and downstream final result interpretation because those belong to the input Derivative nodes and the output result node. I also avoided previously generated field names that the user reported as collisions, and kept the schema focused on how the treated-versus-control comparison was performed rather than the values produced by it.

md_schema.descr: Name of the software or pipeline used to perform the comparative synaptic analysis between treated and control samples. Record the exact computational tool used for this process step. Example: R, Python, Prism, statsmodels, custom pipeline.
Version of the software or pipeline used for the comparative analysis. Record the exact version or release used at this process step, such as 4.3, 1.0.2, or a commit-tagged release.
Family of statistical tests used to compare treated versus control synaptic morphology. Example values: t_test, anova, mixed_effects, mann_whitney, permutation_test.
Design used for the treated-versus-control comparison in the comparative analysis. Record whether the test is paired, unpaired, matched, or nested at the process step.
Name of the morphology measurement or summary metric used as the dependent variable in the comparative analysis. Example: psd_area, synapse_perimeter, circularity, junction_geometry_score.

List of covariates included in the comparative synaptic analysis model, if any. Record the covariates as a concise delimited string or JSON-style list in the value. Example: age, batch, replicate, imaging_session.
Method used to correct for multiple hypothesis testing in the comparative analysis. Example values: none, bonferroni, fdr_bh, holm, permutation_adjustment.
Effect size measure reported by the comparative analysis process. Example values: cohens_d, hedges_g, fold_change, odds_ratio, rank_biserial.
Significance threshold used in the comparative analysis, expressed as a probability cutoff. Typical value is 0.05. Record the threshold used by the statistical test process.
Operational assessment of whether the comparative analysis completed successfully and produced interpretable treated-versus-control results. Example values: pass, borderline, fail.

synaptic_pathway_results.reasoning: This is a Derivative node, so I included only properties of the final computed result object: result file representation, summary/statistical output structure, pathway association labels, direction of effect, significance summary, and final result quality/provenance. I excluded comparative-analysis settings because those belong to the upstream Process node, and I excluded raw feature-table or mask properties because those belong earlier in the DAG. I also avoided previously generated field names reported as collisions, keeping the schema focused on the final interpreted result rather than the method used to obtain it.

md_schema.descr: File or container format of the final synaptic pathway results as stored on disk or in the archive. Record the technical representation of the derivative result artefact. Example: csv, tsv, xlsx, json, parquet.
Filesystem path, object-store URI, or archive location where the final synaptic pathway results are stored. Record the location of the derivative result artefact, not upstream tables or masks.
Type of summary included in the final synaptic pathway results. Record whether the output is a p-value table, effect-size table, annotated comparison report, or combined result object.

Neurotransmitter pathway or receptor pathway associated with the final result interpretation. Record the pathway label used to link morphological changes to pharmacological perturbation. Example: AMPA, GABA_A, NMDA, glycine, mixed_pathway.

Overall direction of the treated-versus-control morphological change reported in the final result. Record the sign or qualitative direction of the observed effect. Example values: increased, decreased, mixed, no_change.

Concise significance summary for the final comparative result, such as whether the pathway-linked morphological changes were statistically significant. Record the outcome at the final derivative stage. Example values: significant, not_significant, partially_significant.
Name of the primary metric highlighted in the final synaptic pathway results. Example: psd_area_change, synapse_shape_score, junction_geometry_delta, pathway_association_score.

Numeric confidence score assigned to the final synaptic pathway result, if the workflow computes one. Record the score used to summarize certainty in the pathway-linked conclusion. Typical range depends on implementation, often 0 to 1.
Operational quality assessment of the final synaptic pathway result object, based on whether the output is complete, interpretable, and suitable for reporting. Example values: pass, borderline, fail.
Version label assigned to the final synaptic pathway results output, if multiple revisions of the final report may exist. Example: v1, final, release_2026_08.
